quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you while driving at night, what should you do?

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch your lights to high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are blinding you, look at the right edge of the road instead of ahead. This helps you stay on the road safely until you pass the other vehicle.

questions.question: What should a driver do if they see an animal on the road?

options.text: No special action is needed.
Honk the horn.
Pass the animal as close as possible.
Be very cautious.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be very cautious.
questions.explanation: Be very careful when you see an animal on the road. Slow down and pass it carefully to avoid startling or scaring it.

questions.question: Which statement is true about passing?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass and check for oncoming traffic.
Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing left.
Wait until you see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror before moving back to your original lane.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When passing, signal at least 100 feet ahead. Always check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for your blind spot. Move back to your original lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Hunting area.
State park.
Deer crossing.
Wildlife preserve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Deer crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down, stay alert, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What is true about driving on a wet road?

options.text: As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
As you slow down, the road becomes more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on a wet road, the less your tires can grip it. At high speeds, your tires may lose grip completely and hydroplane, causing you to slide on a layer of water.

questions.question: How should you prepare for hazards ahead on the road?

options.text: Scan the entire road and all sides of the road.
Look straight ahead at all times.
Keep your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Focus on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Scan the entire road and all sides of the road.
questions.explanation: Your ability to handle dangerous situations depends on spotting problems early. Look far ahead, but also scan the entire road and both sides. Do not just stare at the center of the road.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drugs and driving?

options.text: Any prescription drug is safe if you don't feel drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs can also impair your driving.
Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over-the-counter drugs can also impair your driving.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving. This includes drugs for colds, allergies, and anxiety. It is illegal to drive while impaired by any drug, legal or illegal.

questions.question: Guide signs are ____ signs that show drivers directions and distances.

options.text: Yellow
Red
Green
White

questions.correctAnswerText: Green
questions.explanation: Guide signs have a green background and show directions and distances to specific places. They are helpful when driving in unfamiliar areas.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Left turn yield on green.
One-way.
Cattle crossing.
Two-way left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left turn yield on green.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers turning left at a green light to yield to oncoming traffic. You can turn left when it is safe.

questions.question: When is a U-turn not permitted?

options.text: In a parking lot.
On or near any curve or hill.
On a straight road with clear sight for 500 feet in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near any curve or hill.
questions.explanation: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill. You cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians clearly, which could cause a crash.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn right.
No right turn.
All traffic must go straight ahead.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road joins from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is ahead. A road joins from the right.

questions.question: Alcohol first affects your:

options.text: Vision.
Judgment.
Balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms all the skills you need to drive safely. It goes from your stomach into your blood, then to the rest of your body. Alcohol affects the brain parts that control judgment and skill.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Continue normally through the intersection.
Stop and proceed when a green light appears.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means "caution." Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
There is no need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into your lane when you can see the front of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: If you see pedestrians in an upcoming crosswalk, you should:

options.text: Continue ahead because motorists always have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
Pull to the right and move behind the pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: At a crosswalk, you must let pedestrians cross. Drive when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: You can proceed through a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk when you:

options.text: Slow down to check for cross traffic
Come to a complete stop and verify it is safe to proceed
Stop at least 20 feet before the intersection
Slow down to 10 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and verify it is safe to proceed
questions.explanation: At any stop sign, come to a complete stop before the stop line or crosswalk. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection. Proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol will help the medicine cure a cold.
The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.
There is no effect because they are different substances.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with other drugs can increase how much both affect you. For example, one drink combined with cold medicine could impair you as much as several drinks would alone.

questions.question: Extra space in front of a large truck is needed for:

options.text: Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.
The truck driver to stop the vehicle.
Other drivers when they want to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck driver to stop the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than cars at the same speed. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: When you need to turn on your windshield wipers, you must also:

options.text: Pull over to the side of the road.
Turn on your headlights.
Shift into a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: You must turn on your headlights whenever you use your windshield wipers. Use low beams, not high beams, in rain or snow.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Drive more quickly.
Drive the speed limit, with caution.
Not drive more quickly than 20 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down at the first sign of rain, snow, or sleet. When road conditions are poor, drive slower than the speed limit for your safety.

questions.question: When driving in fog, rain, or snow, use:

options.text: Low beams.
High beams.
Fog lights only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, and snow. High beams reflect off moisture and create glare that makes it harder to see.

questions.question: When being passed by another vehicle:

options.text: Brake hard.
Maintain a constant speed.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a constant speed.
questions.explanation: Keep driving at the same speed when another vehicle passes you. Do not speed up. Let the other vehicle safely merge back into your lane.

questions.question: When you are being tailgated:

options.text: Move over to the right, if there is an open lane to your right.
If there is not an open lane to your right, wait until the way is clear ahead and reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to drive around you.
Never slow down abruptly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle is tailgating you, move right if you can. If you cannot, wait for clear road ahead and slow down gradually to let them pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can
Alcohol does not
Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level greater than 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a tiny amount of alcohol affects your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving skills will suffer. You cannot drink and drive safely.

questions.question: "No zones" are areas around trucks where cars:

options.text: Disappear into blind spots.
Have sufficient space for traveling behind and passing trucks.
Can try to squeeze around the truck when the truck makes a wide turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Disappear into blind spots.
questions.explanation: Large trucks and buses have large blind spots on the sides, rear, and front. These are "No zones." Avoid staying in these areas because the truck driver cannot see you and may not be able to stop or turn safely.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, you should:

options.text: Always insist on the right-of-way over a vehicle when using a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
Enter a crosswalk at any time because it is the vehicle driver's responsibility to stop.
Use crosswalks only if they are convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are coming toward you. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a vehicle that is close may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless:

options.text: You are able to clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle is capable of the speed necessary to pass.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You can only pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street if you can see the road clearly, you can get back to your lane before oncoming traffic arrives, and your vehicle can reach the needed speed. Do not pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: Which of the following about winter driving is not true?

options.text: Winter is the most difficult driving season.
Checking your vehicle's antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels is especially important during the winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is a safe thing to do.
It is best to use snow tires on your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is a safe thing to do.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other slippery conditions. Winter is hard to drive in and needs extra care. Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid often. Snow tires improve your vehicle's grip on slippery roads.

questions.question: When you drive through an area where children are playing, you should expect them:

options.text: To know when it is safe to cross the street.
To stop at the curb before crossing the street.
To run out in front of you without looking.
Not to cross the street unless they are with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: To run out in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down when children are nearby. Children may not understand danger and might run into the street without looking.

questions.question: When your wheels run off the pavement, you should:

options.text: Hit the breaks hard.
Grip the steering wheel firmly, begin to slow down, then move slowly back onto the road surface.
Hit the brakes firmly and jerk the steering wheel hard to pull the vehicle onto the road surface as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the steering wheel firmly, begin to slow down, then move slowly back onto the road surface.
questions.explanation: If your wheels leave the road, grip the steering wheel firmly and slow down by lifting your foot off the gas. Do not turn sharply. Check that the road is clear, then slowly return to the pavement.
